subject: Inequality constraint on sum of parameters via transformed parameters block?

messages.author: ee490f1373633c05
messages.subject: Inequality constraint on sum of parameters via transformed parameters block?
parts:
Hi everyone,

Suppose that I have a block of parameters:
vector[k] beta;
and a set of regressors
vector[k] X;

I want to calculate the derived quantity:
Y <- beta*X;

Is it possible to enforce an inequality constraint such that eg y <= 0?

Perhaps via the transformed parameters block, ie define
real<upper=0> Y;

Thanks!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Inequality constraint on sum of parameters via transformed parameters block?
parts:
On Wednesday, October 14, 2015 at 7:15:47 PM UTC-4, Julian King wrote:
Suppose that I have a block of parameters:
vector[k] beta;
and a set of regressors
vector[k] X;

I want to calculate the derived quantity:
Y <- beta*X;

Is it possible to enforce an inequality constraint such that eg y <= 0?

Perhaps via the transformed parameters block, ie define
real<upper=0> Y;

That is valid syntax but will lead to horrible sampling in Stan and in more complicated cases, your prior on the parameters does not integrate to a constant. A better way to do it is to separate the intercept out of beta (and delete the column of ones from X). Then put a bound on the intercept such that the inequality constraint is satisfied. Like this:

parameters {
  vector[K] beta;
  real<upper = -max(X * beta)> intercept;
}

We have done something a bit like that for a few models and there is still considerable, non-constant dependence between the elements of beta and the intercept. But at least it is a contiguous parameter space.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Inequality constraint on sum of parameters via transformed parameters block?
parts:
That's very elegant --- like the sum to 0 constraint,
only more subtle.

I would like to warn you that this will ensure the constraint
is satisfied for any X in the data you use to fit the model, but
it won't necessarily satisfy the constraint out of sample.
You will need to look deeper into where the constraint comes from for that.

Alternatively, use exp(beta * X) instead of (beta * X) --- that's
guaranteed to be positive. It's what you usually see in things like
Poisson GLMs that require positive linear predictors.

- Bob

parts:
Bob and Ben,

Thanks for the suggestions.

I have used the simple example above to try to explain the problem, but unfortunately my actual model is rather more horrible in how the constraint is imposed (which makes it much more difficult to satisfy).

If you imagine I have y = f({beta_X,beta_Z}, {X,Z}), my constraint requires that y(X+dX,Z) - y(X) < 0, ie the constraint relates to a complex derivative function.

Thanks for your thoughts anyway - it may be difficult for me to enforce the constraint.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Inequality constraint on sum of parameters via transformed parameters block?
parts:
On Thursday, October 15, 2015 at 3:00:30 AM UTC-4, Julian King wrote:
I have used the simple example above to try to explain the problem, but unfortunately my actual model is rather more horrible in how the constraint is imposed (which makes it much more difficult to satisfy).

If you imagine I have y = f({beta_X,beta_Z}, {X,Z}), my constraint requires that y(X+dX,Z) - y(X) < 0, ie the constraint relates to a complex derivative function.

Thanks for your thoughts anyway - it may be difficult for me to enforce the constraint.

You basically have to set up the parameters block such that the inequality constraint is satisfied by construction, rather than relying on the fact that Stan will reject proposals for the parameters that happen to not satisfy the inequality constraint. I would try to basically do the same approach:
  1. Solve for the value of some scalar parameter that renders y(X+dX,Z) - y(X) <= 0 for all observations with equality for one observation
  2. Use that value for an upper or lower bound on that scalar parameter in the parameters block so that y(X+dX,Z) - y(X) < 0 for all observations

You may have to write a function in the functions block that implements (1) because you can't define any intermediate quantities in the parameters block.


Ben
